html:
The Rozvi Empire was a Shona state on the Zimbabwean Plateau, founded around 1683 by Changamire Dombo. The map shows it from 1650 to 1800.

In the early 1600s the Mutapa kingdom had become a Portuguese vassal, and Portuguese settlers raided the plateau. Dombo, probably a Mutapa herder or governor who built a following with royal cattle, beat both the Portuguese and Mutapa in battle and conquered the southern kingdom of Butua. In the 1690s he drove the Portuguese traders off the plateau altogether, pushing Portuguese East Africa back to the Zambezi valley.

The Rozvi built stone enclosures in the tradition of Great Zimbabwe, such as Danangombe, and controlled gold and cattle. They traded with the Portuguese only at fairs they allowed.

The empire weakened through succession fights in the 1700s. In the 1830s Nguni invaders from the south, fleeing the wars of the Zulu kingdom, raided the plateau, and the Ndebele under Mzilikazi settled in the south-west. The last Rozvi ruler was killed in 1866.
sum: The Rozvi Empire was a Shona state on the Zimbabwean Plateau, founded around 1683 by Changamire Dombo. The map shows it from 1650 to 1800.
